whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim, and nothing else. It says who wrote the compliance-path files below and on which issue. It asserts nothing about whether they are correct, and it carries no `reviews[]` entry.
doesNotClaimR2: There is no `reviews[]` entry here and there will not be one from me. R2 wants a named reviewer who is not the author, and I am the author of every path above. This change touches the permission layer (0042 grants DML on directus_* tables whose activity/revision rows can snapshot application row content), so under the team rule it goes to the CTO, and there is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost) -- a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review. The commit carrying these compliance-path files WILL report an R2 violation until that review records its verdict, and that violation is the honest state. The merge-in gate has already refused the unreviewed commit once (commit-msg hook); the change stays staged, uncommitted, until the CTO verdict lands. Writing a `reviews[]` entry naming myself would turn a control into a rubber stamp.
scopeOfTheClaim: R1 only: authorship of the listed paths on AFC-787. It is not clearance of the retention gate (plan 0.10.5), which only the CEO can clear, and it does not record that the staging re-try is safe -- the live Directus boot as directus_app with /server/health and an API round-trip is an operator checklist item (runbook section 8.5), not claimed here. The same staged commit also edits services/staging/README.md (runbook sections 8.2/8.3/7.1/8.5, conditions F1-F5); that path is not in the strict list and needs no claim, but it ships in the same commit once R2 is satisfied.
